elements.element: The licences extend to Customer's affiliates without a written-notice condition.
elements.evidence: Section 2.11 extends the licences to Corio's affiliates only upon written notice to Commerce One. The preferred unconditional extension is therefore not provided.

elements.element: The licences extend to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: No operative language extends any Section 2 licence to contractors acting on Corio's behalf.
Section 2.2 expressly describes the Internal Use License as both “fully paid up” and “perpetual.” No other licence is identified as paid-up.
Although Section 2.2 is fully paid up and perpetual, it is not stated to be irrevocable. The irrevocability language in Section 2.1 applies to the separate fee-bearing Hosting Software License.

elements.element: A subscription licence may not be terminated except for material breach.
elements.evidence: The supplied operative language grants perpetual licences and does not identify or create any subscription licence, so the condition requiring this protection is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated for material breach only if the breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: The supplied operative language grants perpetual licences and does not identify or create any subscription licence, so the condition requiring an uncured-breach limitation is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: The licences are transferable to successors.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 permits assignment in specified merger, acquisition, and asset-sale transactions and otherwise requires consent. It also makes the Agreement effective for only permitted successors and assigns, rather than granting a general right to transfer the licences to all successors.

elements.element: The licences extend to Customer's affiliates upon written notice to the licensor.
elements.evidence: Section 2.11 provides that, upon written notice to Commerce One, the Section 2 licences extend to Corio's affiliates.

elements.element: The licences are transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 permits assignment of the Agreement in connection with a merger or acquisition and provides that the Agreement binds and benefits successors and permitted assigns. A direct-competitor transaction requires consent, but the fallback does not expressly require consent-free transfer.

result.reason: The redline achieves the fallback: it adds affiliate coverage on written notice, while Section 14.1 already supports transfer in an M&A transaction. It does not achieve the preferred position because affiliate coverage remains notice-conditioned, contractors are omitted, the fully paid-up licence is not irrevocable, and there is no general transfer right covering all successors. The only substantive addition is the affiliate clause, so the redline is minimal and does not disturb unrelated commercial terms. Drafting quality is reduced because the affiliate clause does not specify whether the notice must identify the covered affiliates or address responsibility for their compliance.
